examples.en: You shouldn't tease a friend by calling him a liar.

examples.ko: 그 애는 거짓말쟁이라서 아무도 안 믿어요.
examples.en: That kid is a liar, so nobody believes him.

examples.ko: 아이가 거짓말쟁이라는 누명을 쓸까 봐 부모는 끝까지 이야기를 들어 주었어요.
examples.en: Fearing the child would be wrongly called a liar, the parents listened to the whole story.
The shepherd boy became known as a liar.
Don't make me out to be a liar.
I was upset to be called a liar by a friend.

explain: '-쟁이'는 그런 버릇이나 특징이 있는 사람을 가리키고 약간 놀리는 말투예요. 어른에게 직접 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '거짓말꾼'이 있어요.
explain_en: '-쟁이' points to a person with that habit or trait, and it has a slightly teasing tone. Using it directly to an adult can be rude. A similar word is '거짓말꾼'.

examples.en: It's the weekend, so there are lots of hikers on the mountain.

examples.ko: 등산객들이 바위 사이로 난 좁은 길을 지나가요.
examples.en: Hikers pass along a narrow path between the rocks.
A hiker who almost fell off a cliff was rescued.

examples.ko: 정상에서 만난 등산객이 물을 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: A hiker I met at the summit shared some water with me.

examples.ko: 등산객 덕분에 산 아래 식당이 항상 붐벼요.
examples.en: Thanks to the hikers, the restaurants at the foot of the mountain are always crowded.

examples.ko: 시에서 등산객을 위한 쉼터를 새로 만들었어요.
examples.en: The city built a new rest area for hikers.

explain: '-객'은 어떤 곳을 찾아온 손님을 뜻해서 '관광객', '승객'과 같은 짝이에요. 산에 온 사람을 한꺼번에 말할 때 좋고 뉴스에도 자주 나와요. 자기 취미를 말할 때는 '등산을 좋아해요'라고 해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-객' marks visitors to a place, like '관광객' and '승객'. This word is good for talking about people on a mountain as a group and shows up in the news. To talk about your own hobby, say '등산을 좋아해요'.

examples.en: With makeup on, you look like a different person.
After coming back from the army, he became a different person.
Don't ask anyone else; ask me.
The person in the photo turned out to be someone else.
These days that friend has brightened up like a different person.
I mistook someone. It was a different person.

explain: '다른 사람'과 비슷한데 '딴'이 붙으면 말투가 더 구어체예요. '딴사람이 되다', '딴사람 같다'는 성격이나 겉모습이 크게 바뀌었다는 뜻으로 많이 써요. '딴생각', '딴판'처럼 '딴-'이 들어간 말이 더 있어요.
explain_en: It is close to '다른 사람', but with '딴' it sounds more colloquial. '딴사람이 되다' and '딴사람 같다' are often used when someone's personality or look has changed a lot. There are more words with '딴-', like '딴생각' and '딴판'.

examples.en: Conan is a great detective in a comic.
I want to solve problems like a great detective, too.
The great detective found the culprit right away.
As a child I dreamed of becoming a great detective.
The great detective in that novel wears glasses.

examples.ko: 명탐정 셜록 홈스를 좋아하는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: I have a friend who likes the great detective Sherlock Holmes.

explain: '명-'은 뛰어나다는 뜻이라서 명배우, 명장면, 명곡처럼 여러 말에 붙어요. 추리를 잘하는 친구에게 농담으로 '명탐정이네'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: The prefix 명- means outstanding and attaches to many words like 명배우, 명장면, and 명곡. People also joke 명탐정이네 to a friend who is good at figuring things out.

examples.en: During the day, a babysitter looks after the child.
I had to go out in the evening, so I found a babysitter.

examples.ko: 베이비시터 구하는 앱을 써 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever used an app for finding a babysitter?

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 베이비시터 이모를 잘 따라요.
examples.en: My child follows the babysitter auntie well.
I left my contact information with the babysitter.
When I was a college student, I worked as a babysitter every vacation.

explain: 집에서 아이를 돌봐 주는 사람을 말하는 외래어예요. 같은 일을 하는 사람을 '아이 돌보미'나 '보모'라고도 해요. 아이를 맡기는 일 자체는 '아이를 맡기다'라고 해요.
explain_en: This loanword refers to a person who looks after children at home. People doing the same job are also called '아이 돌보미' or '보모'. Leaving a child in someone's care is '아이를 맡기다'.

examples.en: This book is for children, so the print is big.

examples.ko: 아동용 의자를 식당에서 빌릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can borrow a children's chair at the restaurant.

examples.ko: 이 약은 아동용과 어른용이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine comes in separate versions for children and adults.
Children's toothbrushes have soft bristles.
I went to the store to buy a children's bike.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 아동용이 아니라서 아이와 보기 어려워요.
examples.en: This movie isn't for children, so it is hard to watch with a kid.

explain: '어린이용'과 같은 뜻인데, 상품 표시나 설명에서는 '아동용'이 더 자주 보여요. 짝이 되는 말은 '어른용'이에요.
explain_en: It means the same as '어린이용', but '아동용' is seen more on product labels and descriptions. The opposite is '어른용' (for adults).

examples.en: I'm still an amateur, but I practice hard.
That photographer is an amateur, but her skill is outstanding.
I won a prize for the first time at an amateur competition.
I was embarrassed to make such an amateur mistake.
Every weekend I play on an amateur soccer team.
Amateurs and pros differ starting from the amount of practice.

explain: 반대말은 '프로'예요. 취미로 하는 사람을 말할 때는 중립적이지만 '아마추어 같다'고 하면 서툴다고 깎아내리는 말이 돼요. 그래서 일터에서 사람에게 '아마추어 같아요'라고 하면 실례예요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '프로'. For someone who does something as a hobby it is neutral, but saying someone is 'like an amateur' puts down their clumsiness. So calling a coworker '아마추어 같아요' is rude.
